items.content_html:
Summary

Chrome 150 adds support for the focusgroup global attribute, the related focusgroupstart global attribute, and their reflected DOM properties. See https://chromestatus.com/feature/5637601087193088.

This PR adds support for the four features listed above. In particular, for the focusgroup attribute, I've added an individual datapoint for each of the attribute's tokens and behaviors. I have given the behaviors a prefix so they will all be kept together in the BCD table.

Notes:

  • The features are currently listed as non-standard because the spec PR is still open: whatwg/html#11723.
  • I am currently working on documenting only the v1 focusgroup features, which are all implemented. The v2 focusgroup features are currently experimental and subject to change, so I will handle them in a separate project in the future.
  • The WebIDL for the DOM properties is listed in the feature detection section of the explainer.

cc @janewman for technical input/questions. If you could check these to make sure I've not missed anything, that would be much appreciated. Thanks!

Test results and supporting details

Related issues

Update html.elements.input.accept for iOS to mark support as partial.

items.content_html:
Summary

Make the AccentColor and AccentColorText data more regular.

Test results and supporting details

  • Split up AccentColor and AccentColorText. This makes working with the notes much less confusing, since we have to cover just one behavior at a time.
  • Chrome desktop:
    • Shipped the values in version 149, not 150. Confirmed with a test case from Lea Verou — at least for the white/blue anti-fingeprinting behavior.
    • Revised the notes to focus on what the actual behavior is (using a fixed value). Why they did it is maybe something we could mention, but I don't think we typically do this for well-specified behavior.
  • Chrome Android:
    • I don't think either value shipped on Android. Lea's test case didn't work for me and it's corroborated by https://chromestatus.com/feature/5068127364186112.
  • Firefox: This seems to just work!
  • Safari: The original note is a mess (unclear plus spelling and punctuation issues). My own testing seemed to show that Safari just uses the black-on-blue values (changing the setting in the note text had no obvious behavior). Safari on iOS in BrowserStack didn't show anything special (black on blue).

Related issues

  • Initiated by web-platform-dx/web-features#4284
  • Previously: #21150
  • Previously: #30025

items.content_html:
Summary

This is an alternative proposal for #30437.

Basically, the idea this:

  • All values (marked in code in the lists below) are direct sub-features of the CSS property like done everywhere else in the BCD CSS property tree. The support data for these values is whenever the value was first introduced, no matter which context, so their pure first existence.
  • If consumers want to know when the property and all of their values are usable in a specific context, then they can consult the special context_* behavioral sub-features to get that information
  • If a value for a given context is not supported at the same time as the context and has existed before for a different context, the value gets also added to the context as a sub-feature. (this is a special case, and you can see it in effect in the second and third example for stretch and start + end).

This is exercised on three properties:

  • css.properties.align-content:

    • context_block
    • context_flex
    • context_grid
    • context_multicol
    • baseline
    • center
    • end (new from split)
    • first baseline
    • flex-end (new)
    • flex-start (new)
    • last baseline
    • normal
    • safe (new from split)
    • space-around (new)
    • space-between (new)
    • space-evenly
    • start (new from split)
    • stretch
    • unsafe (new from split)

  • css.properties.align-self:

    • context_flex
      • stretch_in_flex (different to the original stretch as well as different to context_flex)
    • context_grid
    • context_position_absolute
    • anchor-center
    • auto
    • baseline
    • end (new from split)
    • first baseline
    • last baseline
    • normal
    • safe (new from split)
    • start (new from split)
    • stretch (the original stretch implementation)
    • unsafe (new from split)

  • css.properties.align-items:

    • context_flex
      • end_in_flex (different to the original end as well as different to context_flex)
      • start_in_flex (different to the original start as well as different to context_flex)
    • context_grid
    • context_position_absolute
    • anchor-center
    • baseline
    • center (new)
    • end (new from split)
    • first baseline
    • flex-end (new)
    • flex-start (new)
    • last baseline
    • normal
    • safe (new from split)
    • self-end (new)
    • self-start (new)
    • start (new from split)
    • stretch
    • unsafe (new from split)

Test results and supporting details

I updated the ordering lint to put the contexts at the top, much like we do for workers or for secure_context_required.

Related issues

#30437
items.title: Restructure CSS properties which contain contexts

items.content_html:
Summary

Add some keys representing a new behavior in module loading, where HTTP errors aren't cached, so developers can now retry loading a module that failed to fetch.

Test results and supporting details

This is a spec change and (I think) one that is impossible to feature detect, so this makes a good fit for a behavioral subfeature.

I didn't test this, but it's well attested through bugs:

  • Chromium enabled it in 156 (tracking bug).
  • WebKit added it with r319474. The Safari TP release notes don't mention it by name, but it was included in the range of changes given by the 252 release notes. When I tried the WPT test on Safari 27, it failed.
  • Firefox bug 2055211 shows this shipping in 154.

Setting the spec URL was difficult. There's nothing in the spec that screams that this should work the way it does, but you can see whatwg/html#10327 and tell me if you've got a better idea here.

Lastly, I added three keys since I believe these are the three entry points for this behavior. See #30304 for further discussion.

Related issues

  • Fixes #30304
  • Prompted by web-platform-dx/web-features#4335
  • Spec change: whatwg/html#10327
items.title: Add retriable module loading keys
